title: S3-CL-05 SIMPLIFIED LCA AND ECODESIGN TOOL FOR SPACE MISSIONS - EXPRO+
description: Following the endorsement of the ESA Ecodesign Policy in October 2025, the systematic integration of ecodesign principles into ESA programmes and projects has become a key enabler for achieving ESA Green Agenda objectives. However, current Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) approaches remain too complex and resource-intensive for routine use during mission conception and preliminary design. This activity addresses this gap through the development of a simplified LCA and ecodesign tool for space missions, enabling rapid environmental assessments and the comparison of alternative design solutions during phases A/B1. The tool developed in this activity will provide a practical and harmonised means to support ecodesign implementation across the European space sector while ensuring consistency with ESA environmental datasets and European assessment methodologies. The project targets bringing the technology to TRL 6.

description: Objective: The objective of the activity is to design and manufacture a fully demisable electric propulsion thruster as needed for low-earth orbit (LEO) telecom constellation satellites.Testing will include on an engineering model of the demisable thruster, and it shall include vibration, performance mapping and an endurance test of significant duration to confirm the design for demisability. Part of the activity is also the assessment and test of critical thruster components for demisability.Targeted Improvements:Enabling a European source of fully demisable electric propulsion thruster for telecom constellation satellitesDescription: In the lastdecades, the amount of space debris has increased substantially, and it is now considered a critical issue by the space community. State of the art regulations and policies are evolving to consider the risks associated to the debris proliferation and increasing launch traffic (e.g. ESA has made a leap forward in the protection of the space environment by issuing a new set of Space Debris Mitigation Requirements (ESSB-ST-U-007 Issue 1).Satellites of large LEO constellations are being requested to become fully demisable under these new requirements. Electric Propulsion (EP) thrusters are the preferred technology for European and non-European LEO telecom constellation satellites to perform orbit insertion, orbit changes, orbit maintenance, repositioning, collision avoidance and deorbiting at end of life. However, large uncertainties remain on the demisability of these thrusters due to the materials used (e.g. high melting temperature materials likeceramics and graphite) and lack of experimental data.This activity will in a first step characterise the demise behaviour of an electric propulsion thruster planned to be used in future LEO telecommunication constellations satellites.The experimental data will be used to correlate and improve the modelling accuracy of the fragmentation process and demiseof critical thruster components during re-entry.The activity will carry out an assessment and revision of all materials, parts andcomponents used in electric propulsion thrusters and develop alternative solutions to make the thruster 100% demisable. Dedicated plasma wind tunnel testing at material/part level shall be conducted for critical thruster components. An electric propulsion thrusters shall be designed with the goal to achieve full ablation during re-entry while retaining suitable performance for their mission application. An Engineering Model of the demisable thruster shall be manufactured and tested to evaluate performance. Testing shall include vibration, performance mapping and an endurance test of significant duration toconfirm non detrimental effects of the demisability.

title: Rehabilitation of the office area at S3F
description:
The increased frequency of Ariane and Vega launches will swiftly highlight the necessity for greater customer availability and office reception capacity for teams engaged in campaign activities. In line with the current expansion, we have identified the necessity to upgrade the S3 area, which would enable the execution of additional satellite campaigns at the EPCU S3B.

In order to meet these needs, it is necessary to replace the existing customer office area at S3F with a new office building. This will modernise the current bungalows, which are no longer suitable for hosting satellite customers. The objective is to be able to host several satellite customer teams simultaneously.

The reception of satellite customers and the management of activities in the S3 zone also require the rehabilitation of the site manager's coordination office in order to supervise the enlarged S3 zone with the ZSE/ZSP.

All of these activities also induce the creation of the PPE store, with the aim of providing local support for operations throughout the S3 and ZSE/ZSP zones.

We are therefore expecting an office area to be set up for satellite customers, EPCU agents, and anyone else who needs to work in the S3 zone, with efficient logistics flows in line with the growth of activity in this zone.

title: ARRAY OF RYDBERG SENSORS FOR MULTI-BAND PNT SYSTEM - EXPRO+
description: Objective: To define and assess the application potential of using array of Rydberg receivers for PNT applications.Description: Rydberg sensors are usually baselined on warm-cell vapour. A finer frequency bandwidth can be achieved with Laser cooled atom Rydbergreceiver, which in the domain of multi-layer multi-band PNT could substantially ameliorate an array of receivers. The objective of this activity is to demonstrate the multi-layer multi-band PNT benefit of using an array configuration of Rydberg sensors. The use ofcold atom is seen as a secondary objective, in case the warm-cell vapour will not be sufficient for an array configuration. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Requirement analysis, including review of cold atom Rydberg performance and definition of use cases. - Trade-off between cold atom and warm vapour cell and selection of use case for Rydberg sensors array - Breadboarding of an array of Rydberg sensors and performance testing - Establishment of a roadmap for the development of an Engineering Model of an array configuration of Rydberg Receivers.Procurement Policy: C(1) = Activity restricted to non-prime contractors (incl.
